en: Every term, formula, and named law the simulator references — explained where you'll meet them.
cur: 模拟器所引用的每个术语、公式和命名定律——在你会遇到它们的地方加以解释。

en: Perihelion / aphelion markers + the live true-anomaly (ν) angle.
cur: 近日点/远日点标记 + 实时真近点角（ν）。

en: Running tally of the gravity, drag & steering Δv spent reaching orbit.
cur: 到达轨道所消耗的重力、阻力和转向Δv的累计。

en: Translucent shell at the body's effective atmospheric edge — Kármán line on Earth, ~120 km on Mars.
cur: 人体有效大气边缘的半透明壳——地球上的卡尔曼线,火星上~120公里.

en: Spin axis + obliquity arc against the orbital plane — the tilt that drives the seasons.
cur: 自转轴 + 相对轨道平面的倾角弧——驱动季节变化的倾角。

en: Inward acceleration that bends the path into an orbit — gravity itself provides it (a = v²/r), so it points the same way as the gravity arrow.
cur: 使轨道路径弯曲的向心加速度——重力本身提供了它（a = v²/r），因此它指向与重力箭头相同的方向。

en: Latitude climate bands (tropical → polar) + how much sunlight this world gets vs Earth and whether its air keeps the heat. Sun is life.
cur: 纬度气候带（热带→极地）+ 该星球相对地球获得的日照量以及大气是否能保持热量。太阳即生命。

en: Where the spacecraft would drift if the engine cut right now.
cur: 如果引擎现在被切断 飞船会漂流到哪里

en: Names the current arc shape (ellipse / hyperbola / etc.) live.
cur: 命名当前弧形( ellipse / hyperbola / 等) live.

en: The constellation figures traced over the nearby stars — patterns the eye projects onto stars that lie at wildly different distances. Neighbours on the sky are rarely neighbours in space.
cur: 在邻近恒星上勾勒出的星座图形——眼睛在距离差异巨大的恒星上投射的图案。天空中的邻近恒星在空间中很少是邻居。

en: The roughly spherical halo of unseen mass around the disc, inferred from the flat rotation curve. It far outweighs the galaxy's visible stars and gas.
cur: 围绕星系盘的大致球形的暗物质晕，由平坦的旋转曲线推断而出。它的质量远超星系中可见的恒星和气体。

en: No global field — only fossil crustal magnetism in the southern highlands. With the shield gone, the solar wind stripped most of the air.
cur: 无全球磁场——仅南部高地存在化石地壳磁性。失去屏障后，太阳风剥离了大部分大气。

en: Nebulae, star clusters, and galaxies beyond the individual stars — the 'faint fuzzies' Messier and the NGC catalogued, each a different kind of object at a different distance.
cur: 星云、星团和星系等深空天体，超越单个恒星——梅西耶和NGC星表所编录的「暗弱模糊天体」，每一个都是不同距离处的不同类天体。

en: Aerodynamic resistance opposing the rocket's motion.
cur: 阻碍火箭运动的空气动力阻力。

en: The hemisphere that never faces Earth — unseen until Luna 3 photographed it in 1959. Heavily cratered, almost no maria.
cur: 永不朝向地球的半球——直到1959年Luna 3拍摄才被看见。撞击坑密布，几乎没有月海。

en: Billboard sprites of ~15 neighbouring galaxies (Andromeda, Magellanic Clouds, dwarf spheroidals) on the celestial sphere at correct RA/Dec — sky-overlay only, not true scale.
cur: 约15个邻近星系（Andromeda、麦哲伦云、矮椭球星系）的广告牌精灵，以正确的RA/Dec绘制在天球上——仅为天空叠加，非实际尺度。

en: Force arrows from each body, log-scaled so all are visible.
cur: 强制箭头从每个身体, 日志缩放 所以所有都是可见的。

en: The boundary where this planet’s gravity dominates over the Sun’s. Stylised radius (real Hill spheres can exceed the planet’s orbit).
cur: 该行星引力相对太阳占主导地位的边界。风格化半径（实际希尔球可能超出行星轨道）。

en: Live numbers (speed, distance, gravity) when hovering a planet.
cur: 当在行星上徘徊时,生命数(速度,距离,重力).

en: Plots the nearby stars by colour (surface temperature) against brightness. Most fall on the main sequence; red giants sit above it and white dwarfs below it, tracing where a star has been in its life.
cur: 按颜色（表面温度）对亮度绘制邻近恒星的图表。大多数落在主序上；红巨星位于其上方，白矮星位于其下方，追踪恒星在其生命中所处的阶段。

en: 71% of the surface is ocean — Earth is the only known world with stable surface liquid water.
cur: 71%的表面是海洋——地球是已知唯一拥有稳定表面液态水的世界。

en: L1 + L2 markers along the planet→Sun line. JWST orbits Earth’s L2; SOHO sits at Earth’s L1.
cur: 沿行星→太阳连线的L1 + L2标记。JWST运行于地球L2点；SOHO位于地球L1点。

en: Concentric shells at fixed look-back times around the Sun. Light travels at a finite speed, so to look farther out is to look further into the past.
cur: 围绕太阳在固定的光传时间处的同心壳层。光以有限速度传播，因此看得更远就是看向更远的过去。

en: Geographic pole (spin axis) vs magnetic pole — the offset a compass reads as declination.
cur: 地理极点（自转轴）与磁极——指南针读取的偏移即磁偏角。

en: Stylised magnetic-field shell + dipole axis. Jupiter’s mag-tail extends past Saturn’s orbit in reality.
cur: 风格化磁场壳层 + 偶极轴。木星磁尾实际延伸至土星轨道之外。

en: Two captured-asteroid moons. Phobos orbits faster than Mars rotates, so it rises in the west and sets in the east; it will break up into a ring in ~50 Myr.
cur: 两颗捕获的小行星卫星。火卫一的轨道速度快于火星自转，因此它从西方升起、从东方落下；它将在约5000万年后分解成行星环。

en: Three colour-keyed body axes — zenith / nadir, prograde / retrograde, port / starboard.
cur: 三个按颜色分类的身体轴——天顶/天底、前向/后向、左舷/右舷。

en: Major moons + orbit rings around each planet (Galilean at Jupiter, Titan/Enceladus/Iapetus at Saturn, the Moon at Earth, Phobos/Deimos at Mars, Triton at Neptune).
cur: 主要卫星 + 各行星轨道环（木星的伽利略卫星、土星的土卫六/土卫二/Iapetus、地球的月球、火星的火卫一/火卫二、海王星的海卫一）。

en: Polar ozone-depletion zones — Antarctic + Arctic — that open seasonally as ClO and BrO catalyse O₃ destruction in the stratosphere.
cur: 极地臭氧耗尽区——南极与北极——在平流层中ClO和BrO催化O₃破坏时季节性开放。

en: Floating overlay with surface gravity, atmospheric pressure, and rotation period. Visible only at planet focus.
cur: 浮动显示表面重力、大气压和自转周期。仅在聚焦行星时可见。

en: Seasonal CO₂ frost over perennial water ice. They grow and shrink as each hemisphere tips toward and away from the Sun.
cur: 季节性CO₂霜覆盖在常年水冰之上。随着各半球向太阳倾斜和远离，它们扩张与收缩。

en: How orbital speed changes with distance from the galactic centre — it stays nearly flat out to ~15–20 kpc instead of falling away, the classic hint of unseen mass.
cur: 轨道速度如何随与星系中心距离变化——它在约~15–20 kpc处保持近似平坦，而非逐渐下降，这是看不见的质量的经典迹象。

en: Translucent rings marking where each body's gravity dominates — an approximation for planning trajectories, not a physical wall.
cur: 标记每个天体重力主导范围的半透明环——这是用于轨迹规划的近似值，不是物理屏障。

en: Sorts the galaxy's stars into the young, metal-rich disc, the old, metal-poor halo, and the central bulge — a fossil record of how the Milky Way assembled.
cur: 将星系恒星分为年轻且金属丰富的盘、古老且金属贫乏的晕以及中心凸起——记录银河系如何组建的化石记录。

en: Earth hangs fixed over this spot — the Moon is tidally locked. Libration lets us see 59% of the surface over a month.
cur: 地球固定悬挂在这一点上方——月球处于潮汐锁定。天平动使我们在一个月内能看到59%的表面。

en: Marker at the longitude where it’s currently noon — the point directly under the Sun.
cur: 当前正午时刻的经度标记——太阳正对的点。

en: Engine force driving the rocket up its body axis.
cur: 推动火箭沿其纵轴前进的发动机推力。

en: Marks the Moon's near-side (always-Earth-facing) hemisphere — the result of synchronous rotation.
cur: 标记月球近侧(总是-地球-变形)半球——同步旋转的结果.

en: Twin tidal bulges raised by the Moon — one beneath it, one on the far side. Two high tides a day.
cur: 月球引起的双潮汐隆起——一个在月下点，一个在背对面。每天两次高潮。

en: Tangent arrows showing instantaneous heliocentric speed.
cur: 正弦箭头显示瞬间太阳心速度

en: In-app encyclopedia of orbital mechanics, transfers, propulsion, mission phases, scales & time, and porkchop reading — every formula and named term Orrery references.
cur: Orrery 内置轨道力学百科全书，涵盖转移、推进、任务阶段、尺度与时间及猪排图解读——模拟器引用的每个公式和命名术语。

en: A 100 km Kármán-line shell separates atmosphere from space; LEO begins another 100 km up. The ozone column at ~30 km blocks the UV-C that would otherwise sterilise the surface — its polar depletion is one of the few global atmospheric measurements visible from orbit.
cur: 100公里的卡门线壳层分隔大气与太空；LEO起始于再向上100公里处。约30公里处的臭氧层阻挡了本会灭绝地表生命的UV-C——其极地损耗是少数可从轨道观测到的全球大气测量现象之一。

en: Earth · 6371 km radius, our orbital perch
cur: 地球·半径6371公里，我们的轨道栖息地

en: Mars' atmospheric pressure sits at 0.6 % of Earth's — enough for parachute aerobraking but not aerocapture. The global magnetic dynamo died ~4 Gyr ago; the residual crustal magnetism in the southern highlands is the only fossil record of when it was alive.
cur: 火星大气压为地球的0.6%——足以进行降落伞气动制动但无法气动捕获。全球磁发电机约在40亿年前熄灭；南部高地的残余地壳磁性是其存在过的唯一化石记录。

en: Mars · thin CO₂ shell + a dynamo gone quiet
cur: 火星·稀薄CO₂大气层 + 沉寂的发电机

en: Lunar surface gravity is 1/6 g; a vacuum-thin exosphere offers no aerobraking, so every mission has to carry full ∆v for the descent. Apollo's free-return trajectory let the Earth-Moon-Earth figure-8 act as a built-in abort path.
cur: 月球表面重力为1/6 g；真空般稀薄的外逸层无法提供气动制动，因此每次任务都必须携带下降所需的全部∆v。Apollo的自由返回轨道让地-月-地8字形路径成为内置的中止方案。

en: The Moon · 384 000 km out, three days each way
cur: 月球·距离38.4万公里，单程三天

en: Search the encyclopedia… (e.g. perihelion, ∆v, porkchop)
cur: 搜索百科全书… (例如 perihelion、∆v、porkchop)

en: Sections for this tab are still being authored.
cur: 此标签的章节仍在编写中 。

en: Motion access denied — enable it in your browser settings.
cur: 动作访问被拒绝——请在浏览器设置中启用。

en: Sensory mode on — try sound, vibration and tilt.
cur: 感官模式已开启——尝试声音、振动和倾斜。

en: Sound, vibration and tilt cues that respond to the physics.
cur: 响应物理的声音、振动和倾斜提示。

en: Hear the physics — cues and ambient tones.
cur: 听见物理——提示音和环境音调。

en: Orrery’s rule is simple: authentic content under a free licence (Creative Commons or public domain), no watermarks, no fan reproductions. When we can’t clear that bar we show the gap rather than paper over it. Provenance for what we did source is on the {colophon}; the insignia live in the {gallery}.
cur: Orrery的规则很简单:自由许可(知识共享或公有领域)下的真实内容,无水印,无粉丝复制品。当无法达到这一标准时,我们会展示缺口而不是掩盖它。我们获取内容的出处记录在{colophon}中;徽章收录在{gallery}中。

en: Representation · colour from catalogued B−V
cur: 示意图 · 颜色来自星表B−V指数

en: A star's colour is set by its surface temperature. We read it from the B−V index — how much brighter the star is in visible light than in blue — which maps to temperature: hot stars glow blue-white, cool ones orange-red. The swatch shows that real colour.
cur: 恒星的颜色由其表面温度决定。我们通过B−V色指数来判读——即恒星在可见光波段比蓝光波段亮多少——该指数对应温度:高温恒星呈蓝白色,低温恒星呈橙红色。色块显示的是真实颜色。

en: Source: NASA · IAU · absolute magnitude {mag}
cur: 来源：NASA · IAU · 绝对星等 {mag}

en: ⚠ Approaching native pixel limit (HiRISE 25 cm/px)
cur: ⚠ 即将达到原生像素极限 (HiRISE 25 cm/px)

en: ⚠ Approaching native pixel limit (LROC NAC 50 cm/px)
cur: ⚠ 即将达到原生像素极限 (LROC NAC 50 cm/px)

en: Interactive 3D model of the Tiangong space station. Drag to orbit the view; tap a module to open details.
cur: Tiangong空间站互动3D模型. 拖曳以引导视图; 点击模块打开细节 。

en: Low-memory mode: list view first. Use the toggle to try 3D.
cur: 低模模式:先列表视图. 使用切换来尝试3D.

en: 3D mode looked slow on this device — switched to the list. Use the toggle to try 3D again.
cur: 3D模式在这个设备上看起来很慢——切换到列表中. 使用切换再次尝试 3D 。

en: Chronological timeline of when each Tiangong module + visitor joined the station
cur: 每个Tiangong舱段 + 访客加入空间站的时间顺序

en: Watch the station's modules join in chronological order
cur: 按时间顺序观看空间站舱段加入过程

en: Build version + deploy date (opens CHANGELOG on GitHub)
cur: 构建版本 + 部署日期(在GitHub上打开CHANGELOG)

en: This footage may be distressing. Continue?
cur: 此视频内容可能令人感到不适。是否继续？

en: This footage shows a fatal accident. It is included for its historical significance. Continue?
cur: 此视频包含致命事故的影像。作为历史记录被保留。是否继续？

en: Films, documentaries, podcasts, and YouTube channels for when you want space content you didn't have to read. Curated for what's actually accurate (or beautifully wrong on purpose), not for what's popular.
cur: 当你想要无需阅读的太空内容时,这里有电影、纪录片、播客和YouTube频道。精选标准是真正准确的内容(或刻意营造的美妙错误),而非流行度。

en: The farthest point of the orbit from the Sun (or parent body). The slowest point — vis-viva: large r → small v. Good place to nudge the orbit cheaply (small ∆v moves the opposite side a lot) but bad for big burns.
cur: 离太阳最远的轨道点(或母体). 最慢的点——相对于viva:大 r → 小 v. 便宜地推动轨道的好地方(小 ∆v 经常移动反面),但对大烧伤不利.

en: The tilt of the captured orbit versus the destination's equator. Polar orbits (90°) see the whole surface every day but cost more ∆v at insertion. Equatorial orbits (0°) are cheap but see only a band.
cur: 被俘轨道的倾斜相对于目的地的赤道. 极地轨道(90°)每天看到整个表面,但插入时成本更高。 赤道轨道(0°)便宜,但只见带状.

en: The angle between a body's spin axis and the perpendicular to its orbit. Earth's 23.4° gives us seasons. Uranus's 98° means it rolls along its orbit on its side. The tilt also sets where the sun rises and sets at landing sites — critical for solar-power planning.
cur: 车体自旋轴与轨道垂直角之间的角度. 地球的23.4°给我们季节。 天王星的98°表示它沿着它的轨道在它的侧面滚动. 倾斜还设定了太阳升起地点和着陆地点,这对太阳能规划至关重要。

en: Public flight records vary by mission. RECONSTRUCTED means we synthesised numbers from secondary sources (trajectory papers, agency press kits, peer-reviewed reanalysis). They're our best honest estimate, not raw telemetry.
cur: 公开飞行记录因任务而异。重建数据意味着我们从二次资料（轨迹论文、航天机构新闻资料、同行评审的重新分析）合成了这些数字。这些是我们最诚实的估计，而非原始遥测数据。

en: Some agencies released only partial flight data. SPARSE flags missions where headline numbers exist but key parameters (like mid-cruise speeds or per-burn ∆v) were never made public.
cur: 某些航天机构仅发布了部分飞行数据。SPARSE 旗标用于标记那些虽然有头条数据存在，但关键参数（如中途巡航速度或单次制动的 ∆v）从未公开发布的任务。

en: We haven't yet researched flight data for this mission. The mission is real and historically documented, but the structured numbers used for visualisations aren't sourced yet.
cur: 我们还没有研究这次任务的飞行数据. 任务是真实的,历史记载的,但用于可视化的结构化数字还没有来源.

en: DLA is the latitude of the spacecraft's outbound velocity vector relative to Earth's equator. It constrains which launch sites can reach the trajectory: a high-latitude DLA needs a high-inclination launch and costs ∆v.
cur: DLA 是航天器出站速度矢量相对于地球赤道的纬度。它限制了哪些发射场可以到达该轨道：高纬度 DLA 需要高倾角发射，并耗费 ∆v。

en: Why declination of launch asymptote (DLA)?
cur: 为什么要解析发射不对称(DLA)?

en: The number adds three pieces: the launch energy needed to escape Earth (C3), the cruise burns to shape the transfer ellipse, and the orbit-insertion burn at arrival (zero for a flyby). Cells in the cheap teal lobe sit near a Hohmann minimum; ridges flag synodic gaps where physics makes you wait or pay.
cur: 该数字增加了三块:逃离地球所需的发射能量(C3),巡航燃烧以塑造转动椭圆,轨道插入燃烧在到达时(飞行器零)。廉价的舌叶上的细胞坐落在Hohmann最小值附近;脊柱上标有线形缺口,物理使你等待或支付。

en: Altitude bands (LEO ≤ 2 000 km, MEO ≤ 35 786, GEO at 35 786, HEO above) trade off ground resolution, coverage, communication latency, and launch cost. Operators pick altitude to match the mission — imaging wants low, GPS wants medium, broadcast wants geosynchronous.
cur: 海拔波段(LEO 2 000公里,MEO 35 786公里,GEO 35 786公里,HEO以上)交换地面分辨率、覆盖范围、通信间隔和发射费用。 操作员选择高度来配合任务——成像需要低,GPS需要中,广播需要地球同步.

en: Inclination is the orbit's tilt versus Earth's equator. 0° (equatorial) is cheap from low-latitude launch sites; 51.6° (ISS) is the lowest inclination Russian launches reach without flying over populated areas; ~98° (sun-synchronous) keeps the same lighting for imaging. It's a constraint, not a choice.
cur: 倾角是轨道的倾斜相对于地球的赤道. 0°(赤道)从低纬度发射场出发,价格低廉;51.6°(国际空间站)是俄罗斯发射在不飞越人口密集地区的情况下达到的最低倾角;~98°(太阳同步)保持同样的成像照明. 是一种制约,而不是选择.

en: Period and altitude are locked together by Kepler's third law. LEO satellites complete a lap every ~90 minutes, MEO every ~12 hours, GEO every 24 hours (matching Earth's rotation). The period decides how often the satellite passes a given ground point.
cur: 周期和高度被开普勒第三定律锁定在一起。低地轨道卫星每~90分钟完成一圈，MEO每~12小时，GEO每24小时完成一圈(匹配地球自转)。周期决定卫星通过某一特定地面点的频率。

en: How squashed the ellipse is. e=0 is a perfect circle; e→1 is a knife-edge ellipse. High eccentricity means big swings in distance and speed between perihelion (close, fast) and aphelion (far, slow) — the orbit feels lopsided.
cur: 椭圆的扁平程度。e=0 是正圆;e→1 是极扁椭圆。高离心率意味着近日点(近距离、高速)和远日点(远距离、低速)之间距离和速度变化剧烈——轨道呈现明显的不对称。

en: The speed the vehicle hits the destination's atmosphere at, after gravitational pull has accelerated it. Sets the heat-shield design — every km/s extra means dramatically more heating during entry, descent, and landing.
cur: 在引力拉动加速后,车辆撞击目的地大气层的速度加快. 设置热屏蔽设计——每增加一公里/秒意味着在进入,下降,和着陆期间加热量明显增加.

en: Extravehicular activity (EVA) is the highest-risk, highest-reward portion of a crewed mission. Suit consumables, micrometeoroid exposure, and CO₂ scrubbing limits cap each EVA at about 8 hours. Total EVA time on a mission is the real measure of how much surface science got done.
cur: 舱外活动(EVA)是机组任务中风险最高、报酬最高的部分。适合消耗品、微流星体接触和CO₂洗涤极限，每EVA在约8小时。一次任务的总EVA时间是真实的测量水面科学完成多少。

en: The orbit's tilt versus the reference plane (ecliptic for heliocentric orbits, equator for Earth orbits). High-inclination orbits cost more ∆v to reach but unlock unique geometries — polar imaging, sun-synchronous lighting, north-south coverage.
cur: 轨道相对参考平面的倾斜角（日心轨道以黄道面为参考，地球轨道以赤道为参考）。高倾角轨道需要更多的 ∆v 才能到达，但能够实现独特的几何配置——极地成像、日同步照明、南北向覆盖。

en: Landing sites are a tradeoff: equatorial latitudes are cheap and warm but low-information; polar sites preserve volatiles (water ice in permanently shadowed craters) and are scientifically rich but costly. Specific coordinates target a geological feature — a crater rim, an ancient lakebed, a fresh impact site.
cur: 着陆点是一种权衡：赤道纬度成本低、气候温暖，但信息量少；极地保留着挥发物（永久阴影陨石坑中的水冰），科学价值丰富，但代价高昂。具体坐标则瞄准某个地质特征——陨石坑边缘、古老的湖床或新鲜的撞击点。

en: The wet mass right after the trans-X injection burn drives every downstream calculation: cruise ∆v budget, structural loads, even the entry mass for landers. Two missions can have similar payloads but very different masses at TLI depending on staging.
cur: 过渡注入燃烧后的湿质量驱动所有后续计算：巡航Δv预算、结构载荷，甚至着陆器的进入质量。两个任务可能有相似的有效载荷，但由于分级方式不同，在TLI处的质量可能差异很大。

en: The average orbital speed. Closer-in bodies move fast (Mercury averages 47 km/s); outer bodies crawl (Neptune averages 5.4 km/s). Vis-viva ties velocity to position on the ellipse — perihelion is fast, aphelion is slow.
cur: 平均轨道速度. 近身移动速度快(Mercury平均47公里/秒);外体爬行(海王星平均5.4公里/秒). Vis-viva 链接速度在椭圆上的位置——近地点速度快,异端速度慢.

en: Module length is constrained by the rocket's payload fairing — the aerodynamic nose cone that protects the module during launch. Falcon 9's fairing is 13.2 m tall; Long March 5B's is 20 m. Modules longer than the fairing simply can't fly on that rocket.
cur: 舱段长度受到火箭整流罩的限制——这是在发射期间保护舱段的空气动力学整流罩。Falcon 9 的整流罩高 13.2 m；Long March 5B 的整流罩高 20 m。超过整流罩长度的舱段无法在该火箭上发射。

en: Mass to LEO is the unforgiving currency of station construction. Every kilogram needs ~9.4 km/s of ∆v to reach orbit; that drives launch-vehicle choice and dictates which modules can fly together. Big modules (Zarya, Tianhe) need heavy-lift; small ones can hitch on cargo flights.
cur: 质量到低地轨道是建造车站的不可饶恕的货币。每公斤需要~9.4公里/秒的∆v才能到达轨道;这驱动着运载火箭的选择,决定了哪些模块可以一起飞行。大舱(Zarya、Tianhe)需要重载;小舱可以搭载货运航班。

en: How long one full lap around the Sun (or parent body) takes. Tied to semi-major axis by Kepler's third law: P² ∝ a³. The further out, the slower; Neptune's year is 165 Earth years.
cur: 绕太阳(或母体)一圈需要多长时间。 由开普勒第三定律绑定为半主轴:P² ∝ a³. 越远越慢;海王星的年限为165地球年.

en: The fastest the spacecraft moves in the Sun's frame during cruise — usually right after the trans-X injection burn or near perihelion of the transfer arc. Tells you the kinetic energy budget the vehicle is working with.
cur: 宇宙飞船在巡航期间在太阳框架内移动最快——通常是在转X注入燃烧后或转移弧近近近处移动. 告诉你动能预算 车辆的工作。

en: The orbit's closest point to the destination after insertion. Low periapsis = closer to the planet (better imaging, more drag) but more atmospheric heating; high periapsis = wider orbit, less heating, more fuel needed to get there.
cur: 插入后轨道距离目的地最近的点. 低近缘=接近行星(更好的成像,更多的拖曳)但更多的大气加热;高近缘=更宽的轨道,较少加热,到达那里需要更多的燃料.

en: The closest point of the orbit to the Sun (or whatever the orbit is around). The fastest point — vis-viva: small r → large v. For comets, perihelion is when the show happens; for spacecraft, it's the cheapest place to do an Oberth burn.
cur: 轨道上距太阳(或所绕中心天体)最近的点。也是速度最快的点——活力方程:r 小则 v 大。对彗星而言,近日点是活跃期;对航天器而言,这是进行Oberth燃烧的最佳位置。

en: Returned samples can be analysed with mass spectrometers, electron microscopes, isotope dating — instruments that are too big or power-hungry to fly. Apollo brought back 382 kg; Chang'e 5 brought 1.7 kg of younger near-side regolith (Oceanus Procellarum). Each kilogram unlocks decades of follow-up science.
cur: 返回的样品可以用质谱仪、电子显微镜、同位素测年仪等仪器进行分析——这些仪器太大或耗电太多，无法飞上太空。Apollo 带回了 382 千克；Chang'e 5 从月球靠近地球一侧带回了 1.7 千克较年轻的风化层样品（风暴洋）。每一千克都能为后续数十年的科学研究打开大门。

en: Half the long axis of an elliptical orbit — the single most important orbit parameter. Pins the average distance from the Sun and (via Kepler's third law) the orbital period. If you only know one number about an orbit, you want this one.
cur: 椭圆轨道长轴的一半——最重要的轨道参数。它决定了行星距太阳的平均距离，以及（通过开普勒第三定律）公转周期。如果你只能了解一个轨道数字，你会希望知道这个。

en: Mass sets gravity, gravity sets every orbit. The Sun is 333,000× Earth's mass and dominates the solar system; that one number, with Kepler's laws, predicts where every planet is at every moment.
cur: 质量设定引力,重力设定每个轨道. 太阳是333,000×地球质量,主宰着太阳系;根据开普勒的定律,这个数字预测每个行星在每一时刻的位置.

en: Both stations sit in low Earth orbit, ~400 km up. Below ~330 km atmospheric drag eats orbital energy faster than the visiting cargo ships can re-boost. Above ~500 km the inner Van Allen radiation belt starts to bite, and crewed-vehicle range drops. The 350-450 km band is the sweet spot.
cur: 两个空间站都在低地球轨道上,高度约为400公里。在330公里以下,大气阻力消耗轨道能量的速度快于访问的货运飞船能重新升轨的速度。在500公里以上,内范艾伦辐射带开始造成危害,载人飞行器的活动范围受限。350-450公里的高度范围是最优选择。

en: Inclination is set by the launch site, not designer preference. ISS at 51.6° is the lowest inclination Russian Soyuz launches can reach without dropping spent stages on populated land. Tiangong at 41.5° is reachable from Wenchang in southern China without overflying populated areas. Each choice trades launch ∆v for ground-coverage range.
cur: 倾角由发射场决定，而非设计师偏好。国际空间站处于51.6°是俄罗斯Soyuz火箭在不将废弃级落在有人居住陆地上的前提下能达到的最低倾角。Tiangong处于41.5°可从中国南部的文昌发射场到达，且无需飞越有人居住地区。每种选择都在发射Δv与地面覆盖范围之间做出权衡。

en: Kepler's third law: at ~400 km the period is locked at about 92 minutes. That's 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets per crew day — the body's circadian rhythm gets hammered, which is why crews live on synthetic 24-hour Mission Time set to UTC.
cur: 开普勒的第三定律:在~400公里时段锁定约92分钟. 也就是每个乘务员日出16天,日落16天——身体的循环节奏被锤打,这就是为什么乘务员以合成24小时Mission Time设定到UTC的原因.

en: 92-minute orbits × 24 hours = 15.6 laps per day, each crossing the day/night terminator twice. Crews see roughly 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets daily. The cabin uses scheduled lighting that follows UTC so circadian rhythm doesn't desynchronise.
cur: 92分钟轨道×24小时=每天15.6圈,每圈穿越日/夜终点两次. 船员每天看到大约16日出和16日落. 客舱采用在UTC之后的预定照明,因此环形节奏不会脱同步.

en: Surface duration is bounded by power (solar charge or RTG), thermal cycling, and crew life-support consumables. Apollo's lunar-day window was about 3 Earth days; Mars rovers ride out years on RTG; static landers usually fail when their batteries drop below freezing.
cur: 地面持续时间以动力(太阳能电荷或RTG)、热循环和机组生命支持消耗品为界。Apollo的月球日窗户大约是地球3天;火星漫游者骑着RTG出行数年;静态着陆者通常在其电池低于冻结时失效。

en: The worlds you can stand on — each built from real data, close enough to look around. Drop onto a surface, trace a rover's path, watch the terminator move.
cur: 你可以踏足的星球——每一颗都基于真实数据构建，足够逼真让你环顾四周。降落到表面，追踪火星车的路径，观察终日圈移动。

en: Getting down is its own problem — and it comes in strict order: leave orbit, survive the heat, thread the entry corridor, and only THEN does a parachute matter. Trade speed for heat, then heat for a soft touchdown, and see why coming home is harder than leaving.
cur: 下降是自己的问题——必须严格按顺序进行:离开轨道、承受高温、穿过再入走廊,只有这样降落伞才有用。用速度换热量,再用热量换平稳着陆,看看为什么回家比离开更难。

en: A bare capsule falling through Earth's thick air keeps accelerating until drag balances its weight — its terminal velocity. For a 2-tonne capsule that's about 46 m/s: survivable in principle, but a bone-jarring hit.
cur: 裸露的返回舱穿过地球稠密的大气时会持续加速，直到阻力与自重平衡——即终端速度。对于一个2吨重的返回舱，这约为46 m/s：理论上可以幸存，但会遭受剧烈冲击。

en: Open a parachute and you multiply the drag area many times over. The same capsule now settles to roughly 10 m/s — slow enough that a splashdown or a crushable seat can soak up the rest.
cur: 打开降落伞，阻力面积成倍增加。同样的返回舱现在减速到约10 m/s——慢到足以让溅落或可溃缩座椅吸收剩余的冲击。

en: Is 10 m/s soft enough to walk away from? That depends on HOW you land: splashing into the ocean or crushing a seat can absorb about 12 m/s, so on Earth — yes. The dense air did almost all the braking for free, and a forgiving landing medium finishes the job. Remember this number: the identical capsule reaches Mars at ~50 m/s — too fast for any seat or airbag, which is why you will watch it fail — and gets no braking at all on the airless Moon.
cur: 10 m/s 足够温和到能全身而退吗？这取决于你怎么落地：溅入海洋或压溃座椅可吸收约 12 m/s，所以在地球上——可以。稠密的大气几乎免费完成了全部减速，而柔性的着陆介质收尾。记住这个数字：同样的返回舱抵达火星时约为 50 m/s——对任何座椅或气囊都太快了，所以你将看着它失败——而在没有空气的月球上则完全无法减速。

en: Why do rockets launch near the equator? Earth's own spin gives you a free head-start, and it's fastest at the equator (it falls off with the cosine of your latitude). Europe flies from Kourou at just 5° north to bank the biggest boost; Baikonur at 46° gives up nearly a third of it. That invisible speed is worth real fuel — and less fuel means a smaller rocket.
cur: 为什么火箭都在赤道附近发射？地球自转会免费给你一个初速度，而在赤道处最快（随纬度余弦递减）。欧洲从仅北纬5°的库鲁发射以获得最大助力；北纬46°的拜科努尔则损失了近三分之一。那份看不见的速度相当于实实在在的燃料——而燃料越少意味着火箭越小。

en: Newton's cannonball: picture firing a cannon from a mountaintop, harder and harder. Eventually the ground curves away as fast as the ball drops, and it never lands. That 'falling forever' is exactly what an orbit is — and it's the very next lesson.
cur: 牛顿大炮：想象从山顶发射一门大炮，越打越用力。最终地面下落的速度与炮弹下坠的速度一样快，它就再也不会落地。这种“永远坠落”正是轨道的本质——也正是下一课的内容。

en: Kourou (5°N) — Europe's equatorial spaceport
cur: 库鲁（北纬5°）——欧洲的赤道航天港

en: Cape Canaveral (28°N) — the US east-coast range
cur: 卡纳维拉尔角（北纬28°）——美国东海岸靶场

en: Wenchang (19°N) — China's low-latitude coastal pad
cur: 文昌（北纬19°）——中国的低纬度沿海发射场

en: Vostok 1 — Gagarin, the first human to orbit
cur: Vostok 1——加加林,第一位进入轨道的人类

en: Earth's atmosphere is dense — about 60 times thicker than Mars's — so a parachute alone can bring a returning crew down to a gentle speed. The only 'extra' is how you spend the last few metres per second: splash into the ocean (Apollo, Dragon) or fire small braking rockets a metre above the ground (Soyuz, Shenzhou).
cur: 地球大气很稠密——约为火星的60倍——所以仅靠降落伞就能让返回的乘员减速到平缓的速度。唯一的“额外”是如何度过最后几米每秒：溅入海洋（Apollo、Dragon），或在离地一米处点燃小型制动火箭（Soyuz、Shenzhou）。

en: The earliest spaceflights were exactly this arc — up on a rocket, down under a canopy. Gagarin even ejected and parachuted separately from his Vostok capsule; Shepard and Glenn splashed into the sea.
cur: 最早的太空飞行正是这样的弧线——乘火箭升空，在伞盖下降落。加加林甚至从他的Vostok中弹射出来单独用伞降落；谢泼德和格伦则溅落入海。

en: Next: reach the Moon — where there's no air to catch you at all.
cur: 下一步：抵达月球——那里根本没有空气来接住你。

cur: Vostok 1——加加林升空并靠降落伞返回

en: Falcon 9 — the booster flips it around and lands on its engines
cur: Falcon 9 — 助推器翻转后靠发动机着陆

en: Every trajectory is the same two ideas at once: gravity pulling down while something coasts sideways. A thrown ball, an artillery shell and a spacecraft all obey it — only the speed is different.
cur: 每一条轨迹都是同时进行的两件事：重力向下拉，同时某物向侧方滑行。抛出的球、炮弹和航天器都遵循这一规律——只是速度不同罢了。

en: Newton's cannonball again: a slow lob falls back to Earth (a suborbital hop), but fire it at about 7.9 km/s and it falls all the way around the planet. Shepard flew the lob; Gagarin flew the full circle.
cur: 又是牛顿的大炮：缓慢的抛射会落回地球（一次亚轨道跳跃），但以约7.9 km/s发射，它就会绕整个星球坠落。谢泼德飞的是抛射；加加林飞的是完整一圈。

en: Freedom 7 — a suborbital lob, the cannonball that comes back down
cur: Freedom 7 — 亚轨道抛物线，炮弹般上升后落回地面

en: Vostok 1 — the cannonball fast enough to circle the Earth
cur: Vostok 1—快到足以环绕地球的炮弹

en: You don't fly straight at the Moon — you coast along an ellipse that just grazes its orbit and let the Moon's gravity catch you. It's the cheapest path there, and it takes about three days.
cur: 你不会径直飞向月球——而是沿着一条恰好掠过月球轨道的椭圆滑行，让月球引力将你捕获。这是去那里最省的路径，约需三天。

en: Apollo 13 turned that same ellipse into a lifeboat: with the ship crippled, the crew looped once around the Moon on a 'free-return' trajectory the geometry handed them for nothing, and rode it home.
cur: Apollo 13把同一条椭圆变成了救生艇：飞船受损后，机组沿几何天然赋予的“自由返回”轨迹绕月一圈，一路乘它返回家园。

en: Apollo 11 — the first crewed transfer to the Moon
cur: Apollo 11 — 首次载人月球转移

en: Apollo 13 — the free-return that brought the crew home
cur: Apollo 13 — 将机组带回家的自由返回

en: Chandrayaan-1 — India's first mission to the Moon
cur: Chandrayaan-1 — 印度首次探月任务

en: Saturn V — the rocket that threw Apollo at the Moon
cur: Saturn V——将Apollo抛向月球的火箭

en: Apollo Command/Service Module — the crew's ship
cur: Apollo Command/Service Module——机组人员的飞船

en: The Moon has no atmosphere, so a parachute does nothing — the only way down is to fire an engine and cancel your entire orbital speed, fighting gravity the whole way. Thrust has to beat weight or you crash. This is the pure case; Mars will hand some of that braking back to the air.
cur: 月球没有大气，因此降落伞毫无用处——唯一下降的办法是点燃发动机、抵消你全部的轨道速度，全程与重力抗衡。推力必须胜过重量，否则你就会坠毁。这是纯粹的情形；火星会把部分制动交还给大气。

en: The margin is brutal: Apollo 11 touched down with about 25 seconds of fuel to spare. Luna 25 (2023) and Israel's Beresheet (2019) got the burn wrong and hit the surface.
cur: 余量极其紧张：Apollo 11着陆时仅剩约25秒的燃料。Luna 25（2023）和以色列的Beresheet（2019）点火失误，撞上了月面。

en: The same coasting ellipse, one frame further out: now everything orbits the Sun. The hard part is timing — Earth and Mars only line up for the cheap transfer about every 26 months, so you launch in a narrow window or wait two years for the next.
cur: 还是那条滑行椭圆轨道，只是再往外挪一个参考系：现在一切都绕着太阳转。难点在于时机——地球和火星大约每26个月才对齐一次，供你走这条省燃料的转移轨道，所以你要么在狭窄的窗口内发射，要么再等两年。

en: That's why 2020 launched a convoy: NASA's Perseverance, China's Tianwen-1 and the UAE's Hope all left within eleven days of each other. The window opened for everyone at once.
cur: 这就是为什么2020年发射了一个船队：NASA的Perseverance、中国的Tianwen-1和阿联酋的Hope在彼此相隔十一天内全部升空。窗口对所有人同时打开。

en: Mars air is thin — roughly 1/60 of Earth’s. A parachute helps but still leaves you at around 50 m/s, far too fast to survive. So every Mars lander adds power: airbags to bounce the light ones down, a retro-rocket or a sky-crane to lower the heavy ones. The right method depends on the mass.
cur: 火星大气稀薄——约为地球的1/60。降落伞有帮助，但仍会让你保持约50 m/s的速度，太快而无法幸存。因此每个火星着陆器都要增加动力：用气囊弹跳缓冲轻型着陆器，用反推火箭或“天空起重机”下放重型着陆器。合适的方式取决于质量。

en: 'Seven minutes of terror': the whole entry, descent and landing is over faster than a radio signal can even reach Earth to say it started. Mars 3 (1971), Beagle 2 and Schiaparelli all show how easily it ends in silence.
cur: "七分钟恐怖时刻"：整个进入、下降和着陆的过程比无线电信号到达地球通报其开始的速度还要快。Mars 3（1971年）、Beagle 2 和 Schiaparelli 都展示了任务多么容易以沉寂告终。

en: Beat the Sun's own gravity. Find escape velocity, borrow speed from the planets, and set a course that never comes back.
cur: 战胜太阳自身的引力。找到逃逸速度，从行星借力，设定一条永不返回的航线。

en: To leave the Sun for good you must reach its escape velocity. At Earth's distance — 1 AU — that is about 42 km/s. Drag the distance outward and watch it fall: escape is easier the further out you already are.
cur: 要永久摆脱太阳，你必须达到它的逃逸速度。在地球轨道距离——1 AU——处，约为42 km/s。将距离向外拖动，看它下降：你所处位置越远，逃逸就越容易。

en: But you do not start from rest. A craft at Earth already circles the Sun at ~29.8 km/s, so the extra heliocentric speed you must gain is only 42 − 29.8 ≈ 12.3 km/s. That is the hyperbolic excess v∞ relative to Earth — how fast you must still be moving once Earth's pull has done its worst. Riding Earth's own 29.8 km/s, that is exactly enough to clear the Sun.
cur: 但你并非从静止出发。地球上的飞行器早已以约 29.8 km/s 绕太阳公转，因此你实际需要额外获得的日心速度仅为 42 − 29.8 ≈ 12.3 km/s。这就是相对地球的双曲线剩余速度 v∞——即在地球引力竭尽全力之后，你仍必须保持的速度。借助地球自身的 29.8 km/s，这恰好足以摆脱太阳的束缚。

en: So you cheat, with a gravity assist. Fly close past a planet and — in the Sun’s frame — its motion changes your speed, by up to twice your approach speed (a full 180° turn is the ceiling; real flybys turn less). And it cuts both ways: pass BEHIND the planet and it flings you forward, pass in FRONT and it slows you down — the same slingshot run backwards, which is how MESSENGER braked into Mercury and how Parker Solar Probe keeps falling toward the Sun. Jupiter, massive and fast, bends the hardest, which is why every outer-system probe flew past it.
cur: 于是你借助引力弹弓来"作弊"。近距离掠过一颗行星——在太阳参考系中——它的运动会改变你的速度，最多可达接近速度的两倍（完整的180°转向是上限；实际飞掠转向更小）。这把双刃剑两头都能用：从行星后方掠过，它将你向前抛出；从前方掠过，它使你减速——这就是同一次弹弓机动的逆向操作，MESSENGER正是靠此制动切入水星轨道，Parker Solar Probe也借此不断向太阳坠落。木星质量大、速度快，弯折能力最强，这正是每一个外太阳系探测器都要飞掠它的原因。

en: Add it up in Δv from low orbit: a strong stage (~8.5 km/s) lands right on the ~8.7 line — the very biggest launches just clear it alone. A flyby supplies the margin and, more to the point, the extra speed to actually TOUR the outer planets instead of limping past escape. That is why Voyager took the slingshots.
cur: 以从低轨出发的Δv累加：一个强力级（约8.5 km/s）正好落在约8.7的线上——只有最大的发射能靠自身勉强越过。飞掠提供了余量，更关键的是，提供了真正巡游外行星所需的额外速度，而不是勉强越过逃逸线。这就是Voyager采用弹弓效应的原因。

en: Leaving the Sun sits right at the edge of chemical rockets: from low orbit the Oberth effect makes solar escape cost only ~8.7 km/s, so the biggest launches (New Horizons) can just manage it on their own. But to reach the outer planets within a human lifetime — and to visit several in one mission — you need the speed a gravity assist adds. That is why the Grand-Tour probes all slingshot past Jupiter.
cur: 离开太阳恰好处于化学火箭的极限边缘：从低轨出发，Oberth效应使太阳逃逸仅需约8.7 km/s，因此最大的发射（New Horizons）可以靠自身勉强做到。但要在人类寿命内到达外行星——并在一次任务中访问多颗——你需要引力助推所增加的速度。这就是Grand-Tour探测器都借木星弹弓的原因。

en: Here is the twist that makes it possible: you do not buy that 12.3 km/s out in deep space. You burn from a low parking orbit, deep in Earth's gravity well where speed is cheap — the Oberth effect. From there the Δv to reach v∞ = 12.3 is only about 8.7 km/s, not 12.3. That is within a strong chemical upper stage — which is exactly how New Horizons launched straight onto a Sun-escaping path.
cur: 让这一切成为可能的关键在于：你并非在深空中获取那 12.3 km/s。你从深处于地球引力井中的低停泊轨道点火，那里速度代价低廉——这就是Oberth效应。从这里出发，达到 v∞ = 12.3 所需的 Δv 仅约 8.7 km/s，而非 12.3。这在强力化学末级的能力范围之内——New Horizons正是这样直接踏上了逃离太阳的轨迹。

en: One engine or thirty? Add mass, add thrust, and let the thrust-to-weight ratio decide whether your rocket leaps off the pad or never leaves it.
cur: 一台发动机还是三十台？增加质量，增加推力，让推重比来决定你的火箭是一跃升空，还是纹丝不动。

en: Launching asks for a Δv; building asks what that TAKES. The rocket equation, solved for mass, is brutal: to carry a payload you carry propellant, and to carry that propellant you carry structure, which needs yet more propellant. Every extra kilo of payload cascades. Watch the curve climb — and note the wall it runs into.
cur: 发射需要一个 Δv；建造则要问那需要付出什么。求解质量的火箭方程是残酷的：为了携带有效载荷你要携带推进剂，为了携带推进剂你要携带结构，而结构又需要更多推进剂。有效载荷每多一公斤都会连锁放大。看着曲线攀升——注意它撞上的那堵墙。

en: That whole stack has to leave the pad, so thrust must beat weight: F = TWR·m₀·g. Liftoff thrust-to-weight sits around 1.2–1.5 — too low and gravity eats your Δv while you crawl upward, too high and you shake the rocket apart.
cur: 整个火箭组合体都必须离开发射台，所以推力必须胜过重量：F = TWR·m₀·g。起飞推重比在 1.2–1.5 左右——太低，你缓慢上爬时重力会吞噬你的 Δv；太高，则会把火箭震散。

en: That thrust comes from engines, and you rarely have one big enough: N = ⌈F ÷ thrust-per-engine⌉. This is why a Falcon 9 clusters nine Merlins, a Saturn V five giant F-1s, an Atlas V a single RD-180 — and why the Soviet N1 needed thirty, more than anyone could control.
cur: 推力来自发动机，而你很少有一台足够大的：N = ⌈F ÷ 单台推力⌉。这就是为什么 Falcon 9 集束九台 Merlin，Saturn V 用五台巨型 F-1，Atlas V 用单台 RD-180——也是为什么苏联的 N1 需要三十台，多到无人能够控制。

en: Here is the wall from the first rung, named: a single stage caps at v_e·ln(1/ε) — about 8 km/s for a good stage, no matter how much fuel you pour in, because you must haul its empty structure the whole way. Orbit needs ~9.4. So you STAGE: drop the dead tank and the next stage starts fresh.
cur: 这就是第一级台阶提到的那堵墙，现在给它命名：单级的上限是 v_e·ln(1/ε)——一个好的级约 8 km/s，无论你灌多少燃料都是如此，因为你必须全程拖着它的空壳结构。入轨需要约 9.4。所以你要分级：抛掉空罐，下一级从头开始。

en: The other way to buy thrust is sideways. When a heavy payload leaves the core short of liftoff thrust, you strap on parallel boosters — Ariane 5’s two solids, Atlas V’s up to five, Falcon Heavy’s two side cores. Crank the payload up and watch how many you need.
cur: 另一种获取推力的办法是横向的。当一个重型有效载荷让芯级达不到起飞推力时，你就绑上并联助推器——Ariane 5 的两台固体，Atlas V 最多五台，Falcon Heavy 的两个侧芯。把有效载荷调高，看看你需要多少台。

en: A rocket is almost all fuel: only ~2–4% of the mass on the pad reaches orbit; the rest is propellant and structure you burn and throw away. That is why one payload can produce wildly different rockets — the designer trades engine count, staging and boosters against the exponential. Many small engines (Falcon 9’s nine Merlins) or a few giants (Saturn V’s five F-1s); one core plus solids (Atlas V, Ariane 5) or a stack of cores (Falcon Heavy).
cur: 火箭几乎全是燃料：发射台上的质量只有约 2–4% 能到达轨道；其余都是你烧掉并抛弃的推进剂和结构。这就是为什么同一个有效载荷能造出千差万别的火箭——设计师在发动机数量、分级和助推器之间权衡那个指数关系。许多小发动机（Falcon 9 的九台 Merlin）或少数几台巨型（Saturn V 的五台 F-1）；一个芯级加固体（Atlas V、Ariane 5）或一堆芯级（Falcon Heavy）。

en: The Soviet N1 Moon rocket needed THIRTY first-stage engines and could not synchronise them — all four launches failed. Sixty years on, SpaceX’s Starship fires THIRTY-THREE Raptors and lands the booster: the same clustering bet the N1 lost, finally won with modern engines and avionics. More small engines, or fewer big ones, has been rocketry’s oldest argument.
cur: 苏联的 N1 登月火箭第一级需要三十台发动机，却始终无法让它们同步——四次发射全部失败。六十年后，SpaceX 的 Starship 点燃三十三台 Raptor 并成功回收助推器：N1 输掉的那场集束赌注，终于凭借现代发动机与航电赢了下来。用更多小发动机，还是用更少大发动机，一直是火箭工程学最古老的争论。

en: The biggest ever built: SpaceX’s Starship on its Super Heavy booster. Thirty-three Raptor engines fire at once — about 76 meganewtons, twice a Saturn V — to lift a ~5,000-tonne stack at a thrust-to-weight near 1.5. And unlike anyone else, it is built of stainless steel: heavier than aerospace aluminium (a worse ε — the first rung’s penalty, made of metal), but cheap, tough, and able to survive re-entry and fly again. That is the whole bet: fly a heavier rocket to get a fully reusable one.
cur: 有史以来最大的火箭：SpaceX 的 Starship 搭载 Super Heavy 助推器。三十三台 Raptor 发动机同时点火——约 76 兆牛，是 Saturn V 的两倍——以接近 1.5 的推重比托举约 5,000 吨的整体结构升空。与其他任何火箭都不同的是，它采用不锈钢建造：比航空铝更重（ε 更差——第一级的代价，用金属堆出来的），但便宜、坚固，且能承受再入并再次飞行。这就是整个赌注：让一枚更重的火箭飞起来，换来一枚完全可复用的火箭。

en: Coming home starts by slowing down — barely. A single retrograde burn at your parking altitude, only ~80 m/s from low orbit, drops the far side of the orbit into the top of the atmosphere. You do not fly down; you nudge the low point into the air and let drag take over.
cur: 返回之路始于减速——仅需一点点。在停泊高度做一次逆行点火，只需约 80 m/s，就能把轨道远端压入大气层顶部。你并非飞下来，而是把轨道低点推入大气，然后交给阻力接手。

en: Now the hard part. You meet the atmosphere at almost 8 km/s, carrying about 30 megajoules per kilogram — about seven times the energy of the same mass of TNT — and every joule must become heat. The shield’s job is to dump it into the air, not the capsule. Come in too steep and the g-load and heating spike (drag the angle up and watch); too shallow and you skip back off into space. That narrow band is the re-entry corridor.
cur: 现在是最难的部分。你以近 8 km/s 的速度冲入大气层，每千克携带约 30 兆焦耳的能量——约为同等质量 TNT 的七倍——而每一焦耳都必须转化为热量。防热盾的任务是把这些能量抛入空气中，而非留给返回舱。进入角太陡，过载和热流会飙升（把角度拉大并观察）；太浅，则会被弹回太空。那道狭窄的区间就是再入走廊。

en: Why the Moon changes shape night to night. Track the geometry of Sun, Earth and Moon and predict exactly what you will see in the sky.
cur: 为何月亮夜夜变换形状。追踪太阳、地球与月球的几何关系，精确预测你将在天空中看到什么。

en: The Moon makes no light of its own — you are watching sunlight sweep across a sphere. The lit fraction you see is ½(1 + cos α), where α is the Sun–Moon–Earth angle: α = 0 when the Moon sits opposite the Sun (full), 180° when it is between us and the Sun (new). Pick a date and the disc shows the real phase for that night — waxing (filling, sunlit on the right) toward full, then waning back to new over about 29.5 days.
cur: 月球自身不发光——你看到的是阳光扫过一颗球体。你所见的受照比例为 ½(1 + cos α)，其中 α 为日–月–地夹角：当月球位于太阳对面时 α = 0（满月），当月球位于我们与太阳之间时 α 为 180°（新月）。选择一个日期，圆面便会显示那一夜的真实月相——渐盈（逐渐充盈，右侧受照）直至满月，随后渐亏回到新月，周期约 29.5 天。

en: Phase is pure geometry: the same half of the Moon is always sunlit; we just see it from a changing angle as the Moon orbits us. Full moon = the Sun behind you lighting the whole near side; new moon = the Sun beyond the Moon, its lit face turned away. It is also why the "dark side of the Moon" is a myth — there is a FAR side, but every part gets about two weeks of day and two of night.
cur: 月相是纯粹的几何现象：月球的同一半面始终受到太阳照射；我们只是在月球环绕我们的过程中从不同角度观看它。满月 = 太阳在你身后照亮整个近侧；新月 = 太阳在月球另一侧，其受照面背向我们。这也解释了为什么"月球暗面"是个神话 — 确实存在一个远侧，但每个部分大约会经历两周的白天和两周的黑夜。

en: The cycle drives more than the calendar: at full and new moon the Sun, Earth and Moon line up enough to raise the biggest "spring" tides — and, when the alignment is near-exact, an eclipse.

en: Low and fast, or high and slow? Pick an altitude and see the trade between speed, orbital period, and how much of the Earth you can watch at once.
cur: 又低又快，还是又高又慢？选择一个高度，看速度、轨道周期以及你能同时观测多大范围地球之间的权衡。

en: Every satellite starts with one choice: how high? Altitude sets everything else. Circular speed FALLS the higher you go (v = √(µ/r)), and the period GROWS (T = 2π√(r³/µ)): a 550 km Starlink circles the Earth every ~96 minutes, a 20,000 km GPS satellite takes about 12 hours. Low means fast, close and short passes; high means slow, distant and lingering.
cur: 每颗卫星都始于一个抉择：飞多高？高度决定了其余一切。轨道越高，环绕速度越低（v = √(µ/r)），而周期越长（T = 2π√(r³/µ)）：550 千米的 Starlink 约每 96 分钟绕地球一圈，20,000 千米的 GPS 卫星则约需 12 小时。低轨意味着快速、贴近、掠过时间短；高轨意味着缓慢、遥远、驻留时间长。

en: Push the altitude until the period matches the planet’s day — 23.93 hours for Earth — and something clever happens: the satellite keeps pace with the ground turning beneath it, hanging over one fixed spot. That is geostationary orbit, about 35,786 km up. It is why a TV dish never has to move and one weather satellite can watch a whole hemisphere.
cur: 不断提升高度，直到轨道周期与行星的自转日相匹配——地球是23.93小时——奇妙的现象就发生了：卫星与其下方转动的地面保持同步，悬停在一个固定点上空。这就是地球同步静止轨道，约35,786公里高。这正是为什么电视天线无需转动，一颗气象卫星就能观测整个半球。

en: So why not put everything up there? Distance costs time. A signal must climb to the satellite and back — at geostationary that is ~72,000 km round trip, about a quarter-second of delay you can hear on an old satellite phone call. Drop to a 550 km shell and it is under 4 milliseconds. That lag is exactly why Starlink and the other megaconstellations went LOW.
cur: 那为什么不把一切都放上去呢？距离要付出时间的代价。信号必须上行到卫星再返回——在地球静止轨道上往返约72,000公里，约四分之一秒的延迟，在老式卫星电话通话中都能听得出来。降到550公里的轨道层，延迟就不到4毫秒。正是这种时延，让Starlink和其他巨型星座选择了低轨道。

en: There is no "best" orbit, only trade-offs. Low (LEO): fast, close, tiny lag — but each satellite sees a small patch and whips past, so you need thousands (Starlink, OneWeb). Medium (MEO): the GPS compromise, a couple dozen satellites covering the globe. Geostationary (GEO): one satellite, whole-hemisphere coverage that never moves — at the cost of distance and lag. Sun-synchronous (SSO): a low polar orbit that crosses each spot at the same local time, ideal for imaging.
cur: 没有"最佳"轨道，只有取舍。低轨（LEO）：快、近、时延极小——但每颗卫星只能看到一小片区域且飞掠而过，所以需要数千颗（Starlink、OneWeb）。中轨（MEO）：GPS式的折中，几十颗卫星就能覆盖全球。地球静止轨道（GEO）：一颗卫星就能实现永不移动的整半球覆盖——代价是距离和时延。太阳同步轨道（SSO）：一种低极地轨道，每次在同一当地时间经过某地，是成像的理想选择。

en: The Molniya orbit is the clever exception: a steep, stretched ellipse that loiters for hours over the far north, where a geostationary satellite (parked over the equator) sits uselessly low on the horizon. It is how the USSR — and Sirius radio — covered high latitudes.
cur: 闪电（Molniya）轨道是那个巧妙的例外：一条陡峭而拉长的椭圆轨道，长时间徘徊在遥远的北方上空，而地球静止卫星（停在赤道上空）在那里只能低低地贴在地平线上、毫无用处。苏联——以及Sirius广播——正是靠它覆盖高纬度地区。

en: The International Space Station orbits about 420 km up — low enough that it circles the Earth every ~92 minutes at nearly 7.7 km/s, roughly 16 laps a day. Reuse the orbit tool, preset to the station’s altitude, and its speed and period drop straight out.
cur: 国际空间站在约 420 公里高度绕行——低到足以每约 92 分钟以近 7.7 km/s 的速度环绕地球一周，每天大约转 16 圈。复用轨道工具，预设为空间站的高度，其速度和周期便自然而然地算出。

en: Here is why you cannot just look up at the same time each night: in the ~92 minutes it takes to go around, the Earth turns underneath by about 23° (~2,500 km at the equator), so every pass traces a fresh path, marching westward. The track itself is a sine — latitude swings up to the orbit’s inclination (±51.6°) and no further, which is why the ISS only ever reaches your latitude if you live within that band.
cur: 这就是你不能每晚在同一时刻抬头就能看到它的原因：在它绕行一圈所需的约 92 分钟里，地球在下方自转了约 23°（赤道处约 2,500 公里），因此每一次过境都描出一条全新的轨迹，逐渐向西推移。轨迹本身是一条正弦曲线——纬度最高摆动到轨道倾角（±51.6°）便不再上升，这也是为什么只有你居住在这一纬度带内，国际空间站才有可能经过你的纬度。

en: And you can only SEE it in a narrow window. The ISS shines by reflected sunlight, so it is visible when it is still lit but your sky has gone dark. At 420 km it stays in sunlight until the Sun is about 20° below your horizon — just past the end of twilight — so look in the couple of hours after dusk or before dawn, when a steady, fast, un-blinking "star" glides across in a few minutes.

en: Where is a planet tonight? It is all about its angle from the Sun — the elongation. Near 0° it is buried in the glare; swung out east it follows the Sun down as an evening star, out west it leads the Sun up at dawn as a morning star. An outer planet can reach ~180°, opposite the Sun — rising as the Sun sets, up all night. Pick a planet and a date and read it straight from the sky.
cur: 今晚某颗行星在哪里？关键在于它与太阳的夹角——即距角。接近 0° 时，它淹没在阳光眩光中；向东偏移时，它随太阳西沉，成为昏星；向西偏移时，它在黎明先于太阳升起，成为晨星。外行星可达约 180°，与太阳相对——日落时升起，整夜可见。选择一颗行星和一个日期，直接从天空中读出它。

en: Why do Mercury and Venus never appear at midnight, always hugging sunset or sunrise? Because they orbit INSIDE Earth's: a planet at a AU can only swing arcsin(a) from the Sun. But their orbits are ellipses, so the leash stretches and shrinks — Mercury's greatest elongation ranges from ~18° near perihelion to ~28° at aphelion, while Venus holds near 46°. Outer planets have no leash at all; they wander all the way to opposition. Inside or outside Earth's orbit — that one line splits the naked-eye planets in two.
cur: 为什么水星和金星从不出现在午夜，总是紧贴日落或日出？因为它们的轨道在地球轨道以内：位于 a 天文单位处的行星最多只能偏离太阳 arcsin(a)。但它们的轨道是椭圆，所以这根「牵绳」时长时短——水星的最大距角从近日点附近的约 18° 变化到远日点的约 28°，而金星则保持在 46° 左右。外行星根本没有牵绳；它们能一路游荡到冲的位置。轨道在地球以内还是以外——这一条界线把肉眼可见的行星一分为二。

en: Five planets are naked-eye, and they behave in two ways set entirely by whether they orbit inside or outside Earth's. Mercury and Venus (inside) are always near the Sun — dawn or dusk objects, and Venus is the brilliant morning/evening star. Mars, Jupiter and Saturn (outside) can stand opposite the Sun at opposition, riding the sky all night at their brightest. Elongation tells you which, and when.
cur: 有五颗行星肉眼可见，它们的行为分为两种，完全取决于其轨道在地球轨道之内还是之外。水星和金星（内侧）总是靠近太阳——是黎明或黄昏的天体，金星就是那颗璀璨的晨星/昏星。火星、木星和土星（外侧）可在冲时与太阳相对，以最亮的姿态整夜横跨天空。距角能告诉你是哪一类，以及何时出现。

en: Watch a planet night after night against the stars and it drifts slowly eastward — except for a few months around opposition, when it stops, reverses, and loops WESTWARD before resuming. This retrograde motion baffled astronomers for two thousand years and is the ghost that finally killed the Earth-centred cosmos. The secret is simple: faster Earth, on the inside track, overtakes the outer planet, so it appears to slide backward — just as a car you pass seems to drift back against the hills. The curve dips below zero exactly when that happens.
cur: 夜复一夜地对着星空观察一颗行星，它会缓缓向东漂移——但在冲附近的几个月里，它会停下、反转，向西绕出一个环，然后再恢复东移。这种逆行运动困扰了天文学家两千年，也正是最终终结地心宇宙观的那个幽灵。奥秘其实很简单：内侧轨道上速度更快的地球，从内圈超过了外行星，使它看似向后滑动——就像你超过的一辆车看起来在群山的背景下向后退。曲线正是在此时降到零以下。

en: Finally, the observer's question: from where YOU stand, how high will it get? A planet peaks as it crosses the meridian, at an altitude of 90° minus how far its declination sits from your latitude. Match your latitude and it sails overhead; sit far to the other side and it skims the horizon, dimmed by thick air — or never rises at all (a negative answer). Same planet, a wildly different show depending on where on Earth you watch.
cur: 最后，是观测者的问题：从你所站的地方看，它能升到多高？行星在经过中天时达到最高，高度为 90° 减去它的赤纬与你纬度之间的距离。当赤纬与你的纬度相符时，它便高悬头顶；若你远在另一侧，它就只掠过地平线，被厚重的大气减光——甚至根本不升起（答案为负）。同一颗行星，随你在地球上的观测位置不同，呈现出截然不同的景象。

en: The Moon's orbit is an ellipse, so it is not always the same distance — it swings from about 356,500 km at perigee to 406,700 km at apogee each month. Apparent size goes as 1/distance, so a full moon at perigee (a supermoon) looks about 14% wider and 30% brighter than one at apogee. Same Moon, a real size wobble you can photograph.

en: Why isn't there an eclipse every month, at every new and full moon? Because the Moon's orbit is tilted 5.1° to the Sun's path, so at most new moons the Moon passes above or below the Sun, not across it. An eclipse needs the syzygy to land near a NODE — where the tilted orbit crosses the ecliptic — inside a narrow ±1.5° window. The Sun reaches a node only twice a year, so eclipses come in two seasons about six months apart. Watch the Moon's latitude dip through the band.
cur: 为什么不是每个月、每次新月和满月都发生食呢？因为月球轨道相对太阳路径倾斜5.1°，所以在大多数新月时，月球从太阳的上方或下方经过，而非正对着它。发生食需要朔望恰好落在某个NODE附近——即倾斜轨道与黄道相交处——在狭窄的±1.5°窗口内。太阳每年只两次抵达NODE，所以食成对出现，两个食季相隔约六个月。观察月球纬度如何穿过这一带。

en: And from where YOU stand, how high does the Moon climb? Like any body it peaks on the meridian at 90° minus the gap between its declination and your latitude — but the Moon's declination swings ±28.5° in a month, far faster than the Sun's yearly march. That is why a winter full moon rides high overhead while a summer one skims the horizon from the northern hemisphere — the reverse of the Sun.
cur: 从你所站的地方看，月球能升多高？和任何天体一样，它在子午线上达到最高点，高度为90°减去其赤纬与你纬度之差——但月球赤纬在一个月内摆动±28.5°，远快于太阳一年的行程。这就是为什么在北半球，冬季满月高悬天顶，而夏季满月却贴着地平线掠过——恰与太阳相反。

en: Here is a trick from Earth's own imperfection. Our planet bulges at the equator, and that extra mass drags a satellite's orbit plane around — usually a nuisance. But choose the inclination just right and the drag turns the plane exactly 360° a year, keeping pace with Earth's trip around the Sun. Now the orbit crosses every point at the same LOCAL time, every day, forever. It works out to a retrograde, near-polar ~98° — which is why almost every imaging, weather and spy satellite flies a sun-synchronous orbit.
cur: 这里有个巧妙利用地球自身不完美的技巧。我们的行星在赤道处隆起，这多出的质量会拖动卫星的轨道平面转动——通常是个麻烦。但如果把倾角选得恰到好处，这种拖动会让轨道面每年恰好转动 360°，与地球绕太阳公转同步。这样一来，轨道每天在每一点上都以相同的当地时间经过，永远如此。计算结果是一个逆行、近极地的约 98° 倾角——这就是为什么几乎所有的成像、气象和侦察卫星都飞行在太阳同步轨道上。

en: The same bulge also swivels an elliptical orbit's perigee — unless you fly at the critical inclination of 63.4°, where that drift cancels and the low and high points stay put. That is the secret of the Molniya orbit: a steep, stretched ellipse whose apogee loiters for hours over the far north (Kepler's second law — it dawdles at the top), covering high latitudes where a geostationary satellite sits uselessly on the horizon. It is how the USSR, and later Sirius radio, reached the Arctic.
cur: 同样的隆起也会让椭圆轨道的近地点转动——除非你飞行在 63.4° 的临界倾角上，此时这种漂移相互抵消，最低点和最高点固定不动。这正是闪电轨道（Molniya）的秘密：一个陡峭、拉长的椭圆，其远地点会在遥远的北方上空停留数小时（开普勒第二定律——它在顶点处运行缓慢），覆盖那些地球静止卫星只能无用地贴在地平线上的高纬度地区。苏联，以及后来的 Sirius 广播，正是靠它触及北极地区。

en: So how many satellites does it take? A higher orbit sees a bigger patch of Earth, so it needs fewer of them: from geostationary, just THREE cover the whole populated globe — the idea Arthur C. Clarke published in 1945. Drop to a 550 km shell and each sees so little that you need a full ring just to bridge the horizon, and thousands of them in many rings for global coverage. That is the megaconstellation math behind Starlink and OneWeb.
cur: 那么需要多少颗卫星呢？更高的轨道能看到更大一片地球，所以需要的数量更少：从地球静止轨道，只需三颗就能覆盖整个有人居住的地球——这正是亚瑟·克拉克在 1945 年发表的构想。降到 550 千米的壳层，每颗看到的范围小到你需要一整圈才能跨越地平线，而全球覆盖则需要数千颗分布在许多圈层中。这就是 Starlink 和 OneWeb 背后的巨型星座数学。

en: One last thread, back to where we started: launching. You cannot reach any orbit from any pad — the inclination can never be less than your launch latitude, and the compass heading is fixed by cos(azimuth) = cos(inclination)/cos(latitude). Aim due east and you get an orbit tilted at your latitude, the cheapest one (why the ISS is served from Baikonur and the Cape). And a sun-synchronous orbit, being retrograde, means aiming SOUTH — exactly why those missions launch down the California coast from Vandenberg.
cur: 最后一个主题，回到我们起点：发射。从任何发射台都无法到达任何轨道——倾角永远不会小于你的发射纬度，而罗盘方向由 cos(方位角) = cos(倾角)/cos(纬度) 确定。向正东瞄准，你就会得到一个以你所在纬度倾斜的轨道，这是最便宜的（这就是为什么国际空间站由拜科努尔和Cape进行补给）。而太阳同步轨道是逆行的，这意味着向南瞄准——这正是为什么那些任务从范登堡沿加州海岸发射。

cur: 每次飞掠接近速度相同（实际辅助链各不相同）

en: Optimistic ceiling — flyby Δv vectors don't add as scalars; a real tour delivers less
cur: 乐观上限——飞掠 Δv 是矢量，不能像标量那样直接相加；真实巡游获得的更少

en: The capstone. Everything you've learned — how to launch, how to leave, how to read where the planets are — comes together in the one job a mission designer actually has: sequencing a trajectory. We plan it the way JPL did on the greatest tour ever flown: Voyager 2, past Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune on a single tank.
cur: 压轴之作。你所学的一切——如何发射、如何离开、如何读懂行星的位置——都在任务设计师真正的核心工作中汇聚一处：编排轨迹。我们将按照JPL在史上最伟大的巡航中所用的方式来规划：Voyager 2，仅靠一箱燃料掠过木星、土星、天王星与海王星。

en: First: you cannot just leave — you launch when the planets line up. Earth and Jupiter align every ~13 months (the window below); that sets when you can start. The rarer magic is when ALL the giants line up so a single craft can chain them end to end — a geometry that fell into place in the late 1970s and recurs only about every 176 years. Voyager 2 caught it.
cur: 首先：你不能说走就走——要在行星排成一线时才能发射。地球与木星每约13个月对齐一次（下方的窗口），这决定了你何时能出发。更罕见的奇迹是所有巨行星都排成一线，让一艘飞船能首尾相连地把它们串起来——这种几何格局在1970年代末形成，约每176年才重现一次。Voyager 2抓住了它。

en: Now the first leg: a Hohmann transfer from Earth out to Jupiter. It costs a departure burn, arrives at some speed, and takes years of cruise. This is the single hop you already know from 'Get to Mars' — a mission is just a chain of these legs, stitched together at the planets.
cur: 现在是第一段：从地球经过Hohmann transfer到木星。它需要一次离轨燃烧，以某个速度到达，并需要数年的巡航飞行。这就是你在"到达火星"中已经知道的单次跳跃——任务就是这些段落的链条，在行星处相互连接。

en: That departure Δv is measured against the Sun, but you start in low Earth orbit — and burning deep in Earth's gravity well, the Oberth effect makes it cheaper than it looks. Wire the leg's departure speed in and read the honest cost from LEO. This is the number your launch vehicle has to deliver.
cur: 那次出发 Δv 是相对太阳测量的，但你从近地轨道启程——在地球引力井深处点火时，Oberth效应让它比看上去更省。把这一航段的出发速度接入，读出从 LEO 出发的真实代价。这就是你的运载火箭必须交付的数字。

en: Here is the trick that makes a tour possible. You arrive at Jupiter carrying all that approach speed — the leg calls it an 'arrival burn' because it is what you would spend to STOP and orbit, but on a flyby you do not stop. You let Jupiter's gravity swing you instead, leaving with up to 2·v∞ of Δv in the Sun's frame (the ideal 180° ceiling, rarely reached) — stolen from Jupiter's own orbital motion, for almost no propellant.
cur: 这就是让巡航成为可能的诀窍。你抵达木星时携带了全部的接近速度——这一阶段称之为"到达减速"，因为这是你停下来进入轨道所需消耗的量，但在借力飞行中你不会停下。你让木星的引力让你改变方向，离开时在太阳参考系中获得高达2·v∞的Δv（理想的180°上限，很少能达到）——从木星自身的轨道运动中"窃取"能量，却几乎不消耗推进剂。

en: Do it once and you save a burn. Do it four times — Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune — and the borrowed Δv stacks into something no rocket could carry. This is the ceiling: four ideal flybys, summed. It is deliberately optimistic: real flybys never hit the perfect 180° turn, the vectors do not add as neatly as a sum, and it counts gross speed stolen, not the rising energy each further planet demands. But even the honest upper bound tells the story — tens of km/s, for free.
cur: 做一次，你就省下一次点火。做四次——木星、土星、天王星、海王星——借来的 Δv 便累积成任何火箭都无法携带的量。这就是上限：四次理想飞掠的总和。它是有意乐观的：真实飞掠从不能完成完美的180°转向，矢量也不像求和那样干净地相加，而且它计入的是窃取的总速度，而非每颗更远行星所需的递增能量。但即使是这个诚实的上限也说明了问题——数十 km/s，免费获得。

en: So: could you fly this on fuel alone? Reaching Jupiter is actually within chemical reach — about 6 km/s from LEO, less than a strong upper stage's ~8.5. But a Grand Tour means ESCAPING the solar system with speed to spare, and that needs ~8.7 km/s from LEO — just past what the best chemical stage delivers. Chemistry gets you to Jupiter and stops; the gravity-assist chain supplies the rest, and the tens of km/s of touring speed on top. That is why Voyager was flyable, and why every deep-space mission since is a plan for borrowing speed from the planets.
cur: 所以：仅靠燃料能飞到那里吗？到达木星其实在化学推进的能力范围内——从近地轨道出发约需6 km/s，低于强力上面级的约8.5 km/s。但“大巡游”意味着带着富余的速度逃离太阳系，这需要从近地轨道出发约8.7 km/s——刚好超出最好的化学火箭级所能提供的。化学推进能把你送到木星，然后就到此为止；其余的速度由引力辅助链提供，外加数十 km/s 的巡游速度。这就是Voyager能够成行的原因，也是此后每一次深空任务都是一个向行星借速度的计划的原因。

en: This is how real missions are designed: a launch window set by the planets, a chain of transfer legs, and gravity assists to buy the Δv chemistry cannot. Voyager 2 remains the only spacecraft to visit all four giant planets — on a route that existed for a 176-year moment. Cassini took the opposite tack: four assists (Venus twice, Earth, Jupiter) that first sent it INWARD to build speed before flinging it out to Saturn.
cur: 真实任务就是这样设计的：由行星决定的发射窗口、一连串转移航段，以及用引力辅助来换取化学推进无法提供的Δv。Voyager 2至今仍是唯一造访全部四颗巨行星的航天器——走的是一条只在176年一瞬中存在的路线。Cassini则反其道而行：四次辅助（两次金星、地球、木星）先把它送向内侧积累速度，再甩向土星。

en: In 1965 Gary Flandro, a Caltech graduate student working at JPL, noticed the outer planets would line up in the late 1970s so a single craft could tour them all — a coincidence that would not repeat until 2153. That observation became Voyager.

en: Coming home, you cannot just aim at the ground — you must thread a corridor of entry angles. Too shallow and your trajectory's perigee stays above the thick air: you graze the top and SKIP back into space, like a stone off a pond. Too steep and the deceleration spikes past what a body — or a hull — can take. From low orbit at 7.8 km/s the corridor is generous (you are too slow to skip). But drop in from the MOON at 11 km/s and the ballistic corridor vanishes: any angle shallow enough to not skip pulls over 30 g. That is why Apollo did not fall like a brick — it flew a LIFTING entry, tilting its offset centre of mass to steer, threading a corridor barely 2° wide.
cur: 返回地球时，你不能只瞄准地面——你必须穿过一条由再入角构成的走廊。角度太浅，轨迹的近地点会停留在稠密大气之上：你擦过顶部并弹回太空，就像水漂石子。角度太陡，减速峰值会超过人体——或舱体——所能承受的极限。从7.8 km/s的低轨道返回时走廊很宽裕（你太慢，弹不出去）。但从月球以11 km/s切入，弹道走廊便荡然无存：任何浅到不会弹出的角度都会带来超过30 g的过载。这就是为什么Apollo没有像砖头一样直落——它飞的是升力式再入，通过倾斜偏置质心来操纵方向，穿过一条仅约2°宽的走廊。

en: So WHEN do you leave? Every departure date and cruise duration costs a different amount of fuel, and the way to see them all at once is the chart mission designers actually use: the porkchop plot. Each cell here is a real solution of Lambert's problem — given where Earth is on this day and where Mars will be after that many days of flight, what single transfer orbit connects them, and what Δv does it cost? The cool valleys are the launch windows; the crosshair is the single cheapest date-and-duration to go. Miss the valley and the fuel climbs a wall — which is why a Mars launch window opens for only a few weeks every 26 months.
cur: 那么，你该何时出发？每个出发日期和巡航时长所需的燃料各不相同，而要一次看清全部方案，就得用任务设计师真正使用的图表：porkchop 图。这里的每个格子都是 Lambert 问题的真实解——已知地球在这一天的位置，以及火星在飞行若干天后所处的位置，哪条转移轨道能将二者连接，又需要多少 Δv？那些凉色的低谷就是发射窗口，十字准线标出的是最省的日期与时长组合。错过低谷，燃料需求便如撞墙般飙升——这正是火星发射窗口每 26 个月只开启短短几周的原因。
